focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	I help run a neighborhood arts group that has borrowed classrooms and church halls for six years.
e002	A landlord has offered us a visible storefront on a five-year lease at below-market rent, but even the discounted rent would use almost half our unrestricted budget.
e003	Several teaching artists want a permanent home because moving materials is exhausting and participants never know where to find us.
e004	Our treasurer thinks a lease could turn the group into a building-maintenance organization.
e005	I want the stability and visibility, but I cannot tell whether the space would serve the program or slowly become the program.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e006	The storefront could solve real access and coordination problems while creating a fixed cost that changes what the organization must prioritize.
e007	Below-market rent is not automatically affordable if it consumes flexibility or requires growth to sustain it.
e008	Identify which benefits require a permanent address and which could come from better scheduling, storage, or a shorter agreement.
e009	The governance question matters too: who can reduce programming or raise money when the building demands it?
[Turn 7 USER]
e050	I am leaning toward accepting the six-month license and running three recurring programs rather than treating the storefront as an open-ended community center.
e051	I will recommend the five-year lease only if we finish the license with twelve months of rent committed, stable artist fees, and evidence that regular participants use the space beyond special events.
e052	I am willing to close the storefront after six months if those conditions fail, but I am not sure the rest of the board or the teaching artists will accept that after families have formed routines.
e053	I still worry that the pilot can measure use and workload without measuring the reputational cost of leaving.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e054	Your position separates accepting a bounded license from willingness to recommend the long lease.
e055	The funding, fee, and use conditions make the later decision inspectable, while the narrow program scope limits some expectation.
e056	The unresolved issue is collective willingness to honor an exit rule once real relationships exist.
e057	The pilot can reveal use and operating burden; it cannot make departure reputationally neutral or guarantee that the board will follow today's criteria.
